newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-News sparks media/telecom moves.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-News sparks media/telecom moves.

text.p: Several news reports in the media and telecommunications industry sparked some activity in bonds for those sectors Tuesday on an otherwise quiet day of trading in the U.S. corporate bond market, traders said.
Reports that News Corp won a tentative accord to join PrimeStar Partners, the second largest U.S. direct broadcast satellite (DBS) provider, stirred junk bonds from DBS companies.
Bonds of TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc (TSAT), which owns a 21 percent stake in the PrimeStar partners, rose 1 1/4 point to 57 1/2-58 on the news, traders said.
Analysts said PrimeStar would be able to upgrade its DBS services more quickly if it obtained access to orbital slots and licences owned by News Corp.
Meanwhile, the bonds of EchoStar Communications Corp dropped only one point on the news, traders said. Very few EchoStar bonds traded on Tuesday, they added.
A deal for News Corp to acquire EchoStar, the third largest U.S. DBS provider, fell apart several weeks ago.
High-grade traders said spreads on News Corp bonds, rated Baa3/BBB, tightened around two basis points on the news.

Elsewhere, investors in telecommunications credits struggled to access the impact of reports that AT&T Corp, the largest U.S. long-distance telephone company, is in talks to aquire SBC Communications Corp, a local telephone provider.
If completed, the $50 billion deal would be the largest merger in history and would have widespread repercussions on the evolving telecommunications landscape in the U.S.
"I don't think investors have been able to form hard and fast opionions on this," said Douglas Conn, high-yield bond telecommunications analyst at Lehman Brothers Inc.
Traders said spreads on AT&T bonds tightened approximately one basis point on the news, while spreads on SBC bonds, which rarely trade, were unchanged.
Activity was more brisk in junk bonds, where telecommunications credits were off by approximately 1/2 a point on the day, traders said.
Volume in more liquid issues from competitive local exchange carriers (CLECs) such as Brooks Fiber Properties Inc and Teleport Communications Group was heavy.
Conn believed the softness in the sector may have resulted from a weak Treasury market, rather than from the merger news.
Conn expected an AT&T/SBC merger would have a mixed impact on fortunes of CLECs.

He said a combined AT&T/SBC would create a more formidable competitor for the CLECS in the short run. However, over the long term, it would also make some CLECs more attractive acquisition candidates as the entire industry consolidates.
In the broader markets, high-yield bond prices weakened an average of 1/8 to 1/4 of a point on very light trading.
High-grade bond spreads remained largely unchanged.

However, one high-grade trader said, "Ever since the Federal Reserve passed on hiking interest rates, we have seen solid buying. A lot of people were on the sidelines and have since come back into the market."
In the stock market, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 37.50 points to end the day at 7383.41.
U.S. Treasuries closed moderately lower on rumors of hedge fund selling and renewed fears that the Fed will raise rates again in July.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury dropped 16/32 to 94-31/32. Its yield rose to 7.03 percent.
-Douglas Brown, 212-859-1662
